label: Qwen3-TTS local voice-generation adapter
summary: Use Qwen3-TTS VoiceDesign or CustomVoice as an optional local instrument for original spoken or character cues, with no private voice uploaded and no child or living-artist imitation assumed.

handoffs.label: Generate bounded original voice cues
handoffs.intent: Make short, song-local spoken or character cues whose tone, rhythm, emotional direction, and optional declared pitch treatment support an authored arrangement.
inputs: A song-relative lyric or cue list and one player-facing voice description
An explicit model id, seed, language, output role, and rights note
For pitch correction: an explicit key, scale, preset, and musical reason; never a silently inferred key
Only an owned or synthetic reference voice when voice cloning is deliberately authorized
outputs: New lossless WAV cues outside recordings/raw and FINAL
A sidecar recording exact model id, mode, seed, prompt, device, sample rate, output checksums, and license note
When tuning is requested, preserved raw cues plus per-cue autotune settings, analysis, and checksums
steps: Run `PATH=.eprs-local/qwen3-tts/bin:$PATH eprs doctor --workflow local-voice-collaboration` and inspect the exact Qwen3-TTS model card and license before generation.
Use VoiceDesign or CustomVoice for an original character by default; do not upload family voices or use a child's voice.
Generate the smallest useful cue set, preserve every candidate, and compare the cues in the complete arrangement.
For an audible tuned character, use the runner's `--autotune-preset` controls or render alternatives with `eprs autotune`; read `docs/VOCALS.md` and describe behavior rather than naming an artist.
Bring only a musically useful candidate into an experiment or mix; generated audio is not automatically approved or cleared for release.
verification: Confirm every raw and processed output opens, has the declared duration/sample rate/channels, is not clipped or truncated, and matches its recorded checksum.
For tuning, confirm voiced-frame coverage and target notes, then compare raw and tuned cues at matched level in stereo and mono.
Confirm the generated voice is synthetic or consent-cleared, the source prompt is preserved, and no model result is presented as a human performance or release approval.

preserve: The editable cue list, model/version, seed, instruction, generated candidates, checksums, and exact rights/license context
The distinction between synthetic character voice, consented human voice, and external reference material
avoid: Uploading private family or child recordings, imitating a living artist or identifiable child, hiding failed generations, or copying a reference performance
Treating an Apache-2.0 code/weight license as a blanket clearance for every input, dataset, voice, or downstream use
